title: Paranormal Activity on Broadway #paranormalactivityplay #paranormalac...
transcript: The scariest part about this horror play is how toxic the relationship is between the two central characters. Paranormal Activity on Broadway is a suspense thriller about Louise and Jimmy, a young married couple who, having just moved to London, are terrified to rediscover the same hauntings that plagued them back in Chicago. At first, Jimmy's convinced that it's all in Lou's head, and his gaslighting only subsides once he's sufficiently spooked as well, in arguably the best illusion of the entire show. The plot is nothing to write home about, but it's an apt premise for the genre and it's convincingly performed. Creating an immediate and scary experience in such a large venue is a difficult assignment, and in this case I felt that the suspense and anticipation were scarier than the actual scares. However, the tension is impressively taught, especially in Act 2, rendering you on edge and susceptible to the jump scares even when they aren't super surprising. While the show doesn't depict the same story as the 2005 film, it has film-like sensibilities that movie buffs and horror fans alike will appreciate. There are tons of details to pick apart and analyze that aren't essential to enjoying the piece but give it a rewatchability factor and will delight the Reddit theorists. If I go back for a second viewing, I'll try for a better seat. The production has disappointingly egregious sightlines. From the side, there are lots of moments where you'll hear the audience react to things that you can't see. Despite being so close, I felt like I was in one of the worst seats in the house, and it honestly doesn't seem like there are that many great ones, given the set design. Setting that aside, I would say this more or less delivers on its promises. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
